Defence in depth.d: A security approach that uses several independent layers of protection, so an attacker (or a mistake) has to get past all of them before harm is done.

Supply chain attack.d: An attack that targets something you install or depend on, such as a plugin, package or MCP server, instead of attacking you directly.

AI review board.d: A small cross-functional group that reviews new uses of AI before launch, sorts them by risk and keeps an eye on existing ones.

Automation bias.d: The human tendency to over-trust suggestions from an automated system, so that reviewers approve outputs without really checking them.

Counterfactual test.d: A test that changes one detail of an input that shouldn't matter, such as a name or pronoun, and checks that the output stays the same.

Demographic parity.d: A fairness measure that asks whether each group receives a positive outcome (such as approval) at the same rate.

Catastrophic forgetting.d: When fine-tuning a model on a narrow task makes it noticeably worse at things it could do before.

Continued pre-training.d: Extra next-token training of an existing model on large amounts of unlabelled text from one domain, before or instead of fine-tuning.

Hyperparameter.d: A setting chosen before training rather than learned from data, such as the number of epochs, the learning rate or the batch size.

LoRA.d: Low-Rank Adaptation: a fine-tuning method that freezes the model's weights and trains two small extra matrices per layer, producing a small adapter file.

PEFT.d: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning: methods such as LoRA that adapt a model by training only a small number of new or selected parameters.

Reinforcement fine-tuning.d: Fine-tuning in which the model's answers are scored by a grader or reward function, and the model is trained to earn higher scores.
